title: Scheduler: add workload signals (prompt length buckets, streaming flag, concurrency) to batching heuristics
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Goal
Add a minimal, low-cardinality set of workload signals into the scheduler decision inputs so tiered batching defaults can be workload-aware without per-tenant autotuning.

This ticket is explicitly about (a) extracting/deriving signals and (b) plumbing them into the scheduler heuristics interface. It is not the final tuning of tier knob values (fast/standard/cost-efficient) — that’s handled in the tier profile work and follow-on tuning tickets.

Why
Our current continuous batching heuristics mostly operate on queue state (tokens waiting, active sequences, etc.). For tier defaults, we need to avoid common foot-guns:
- Mixed prompt-length traffic can starve long-prefill requests or blow up tail latency for short prompts depending on current batching behavior.
- Streaming routes have different sensitivity: users notice inter-token delay/jitter more than pure throughput.
- Concurrency shape (bursty vs steady high parallelism) should influence max-wait behavior and batch assembly choices.

Scope (signals)
1) Prompt length buckets
- Use prompt token count (prefill tokens) to map requests into coarse buckets for heuristic selection.
- Buckets should be stable across model families and keep telemetry cardinality bounded.
- Proposed initial buckets (prefill tokens):
  - B0: 0–127
  - B1: 128–511
  - B2: 512–2047
  - B3: 2048+

2) Streaming flag
- Boolean: streaming=true when request is a streaming response (SSE/websocket) vs non-streaming.
- Scheduler should treat streaming requests differently for fairness + inter-token latency (ITL) protection.

3) Concurrency signal
- Provide a coarse-grained measure of concurrent in-flight sequences for the route/model worker.
- The heuristic needs a stable “load level” input, not exact tenant concurrency.
- Proposed: a small enum derived from observed concurrent sequences at dispatch time:
  - C0: 1–2
  - C1: 3–8
  - C2: 9–32
  - C3: 33+

Non-goals
- No per-tenant learned policy / online tuning.
- No cross-region routing changes.
- Do not add high-cardinality labels to metrics (must comply with the new tier label cardinality controls).

Implementation notes / design decisions
- Signal extraction point: as early as possible in request admission / enqueue path so decisions are made consistently and can be traced.
- Prompt tokens should be computed from the request payload using our existing token counting utility in the API layer OR from the already-parsed tokenized prompt in runtime (prefer runtime if available to avoid duplicating tokenization work).
- Concurrency should be sampled from scheduler state (active sequences + queued) at request enqueue time. We should explicitly define whether we use “active” only or “active + queued”; for initial heuristics we’ll use active sequences (decode-active + prefill-active) to represent the effective GPU contention.
- Streaming flag should be plumbed end-to-end in the request context (control plane -> worker -> scheduler), not re-inferred.

Scheduler API changes
- Extend scheduler decision input struct with:
  - prompt_len_bucket
  - is_streaming
  - concurrency_bucket
- The decision inputs should be stored alongside the request for later reason-code emission and tracing (ENG-18426).

Observability requirements (coordination)
- We need internal metrics to validate signals and catch regressions without exploding cardinality.
- Add counters/histograms WITHOUT per-request IDs:
  - scheduler.request_prompt_len_bucket_count{bucket}
  - scheduler.request_streaming_count{streaming=true|false}
  - scheduler.request_concurrency_bucket_count{bucket}
  - scheduler.batch_assembly_by_bucket (sampled) — only if we can do it with bounded labels and sampling.
- Any metrics that combine tier + model + region + bucket need to be evaluated for cardinality; default to tracing for detailed debugging.

Acceptance criteria
- Request context includes prompt length bucket + streaming boolean + concurrency bucket.
- Scheduler heuristics have access to these signals and can branch logic on them (even if initial branch logic is a no-op behind a flag).
- Unit tests cover:
  - bucket boundaries
  - streaming propagation
  - concurrency bucketing stability
- Integration test / perf harness smoke test demonstrates signals being emitted (logs/traces) for mixed workload scenarios.
- No measurable overhead in the hot path (>1% CPU increase in request admission) on representative load test.

Links
- GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr-28445-scheduler-use-streaming-and-length-buckets.json
- Related tickets: ENG-18422 (schema), ENG-18426 (reason codes), ENG-18427 (mixed workload perf suite)

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: token counting adds latency or CPU overhead.
  - Mitigation: use already-computed token counts when available; otherwise compute once and cache in request context.
- Risk: concurrency bucket flaps causing unstable behavior.
  - Mitigation: keep buckets coarse; consider smoothing (EMA) later if needed.
- Risk: metrics cardinality blow-up.
  - Mitigation: keep labels minimal; rely on tracing for detail; coordinate with telemetry standards and cardinality controls.

Rollout plan (for this ticket)
- Land signal plumbing behind a runtime flag (enabled in canary first).
- Confirm traces show correct signal values and that no additional high-cardinality labels are emitted.
- After validation, enable by default (still no behavior changes unless the tiered defaults feature flag is enabled).
comments: 2026-01-16 (Sofia Ivanova): Marking P0 since tier defaults can’t be meaningfully “workload-aware” without these signals. Please keep buckets coarse and stable; we can revise after we see real traffic distributions.

2026-01-20 (Marcus Reed): Drafted initial bucket ranges for prompt lengths. Question: do we bucket by prompt tokens only, or prompt+expected_output? Proposal: prompt-only for now; expected output is too noisy at admission time and varies by stop conditions.

2026-01-24 (Omar El-Sayed): For streaming, please ensure we’re capturing a boolean that reflects actual streaming transport, not just “stream=true” in API params. We’ve seen misconfig where clients request streaming but don’t consume; would be good to represent server-side streaming mode.

2026-01-25 (Julian Moore): Concurrency definition matters. Suggest concurrency=active_sequences (prefill+decode) rather than queued length. Queue depth is already in heuristics; we want a new signal that captures GPU contention level.

2026-02-02 (Allison Grant): On metrics: avoid tier*bucket*model*route combinations. If you need per-route debugging, put it in tracing spans with sampling. A single histogram with bucket label is fine.
2026-02-09 (Marcus Reed): Implemented signal struct + plumbing locally; token count reused from existing parsed request in worker. Added unit tests for bucket boundaries. Pushing PR shortly.

2026-02-11 (Marcus Reed): Opened PR: redwood/pr-28445 (scheduler use streaming and length buckets). Includes concurrency bucket with four coarse levels and trace attributes (not metric labels) for bucket + streaming. Metrics are counts per bucket only.

2026-02-18 (Rafael Mendes): Canary note: please add a guard so if token count is unavailable we default to a safe bucket and emit a debug log once per minute (rate limited). We don’t want missing signals to crash admission.
2026-02-20 (Marcus Reed): Updated PR with fallback behavior: unknown token count => B2 (512–2047) conservative default; added rate-limited warning + tracing field ‘prompt_len_bucket_source=unknown’.
2026-02-26 (Sahana Iyer): CI GPU perf jobs passed; no measurable overhead in admission on synthetic test. Mixed workload scenarios still pending in benchmark-lab (ENG-18427).

2026-03-03 (Sofia Ivanova): Approved. Make sure ENG-18426 consumes the stored decision inputs rather than recomputing. Also ensure the flag defaults to on only when tiered defaults flag is enabled (avoid changing behavior prematurely).

2026-03-07 (Marcus Reed): Merged PR-28445. Signals are plumbed and available to heuristics; behavior is still gated. Marking ticket Done; follow-up tuning will happen under fast-tier and cost-efficient tier tickets.
